title: Cross-SDK: connection pool & timeout defaults + streaming retry ergonomics
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: converge Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs on safe, production-friendly transport defaults for keep-alive, connection pooling, and request timeouts, and improve streaming retry ergonomics so developers can handle transient errors without leaks or unexpected hangs.

Scope: cross-SDK RFC + implementation work across Python, Node, and Go clients. Deliverables: 1) recommended default values for TCP keep-alive, http/2 connection pool size, and per-request/connect/read timeouts; 2) standardized config surface across SDKs (env + programmatic); 3) streaming client API changes to expose explicit retryable streaming checkpoints and cancellation tokens; 4) integration tests and benchmark harness for representative workloads.

Non-goals: full protocol redesign, breaking backward incompatible APIs without migration plan, server-side runtime changes.

Acceptance criteria: 
- SDKs expose consistent config keys: REDWOOD_HTTP_TIMEOUT, REDWOOD_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, REDWOOD_KEEPALIVE, REDWOOD_MAX_IDLE_CONNS.
- Out-of-the-box defaults protect against long-lived hung streams and excessive idle connections under heavy concurrent usage.
- Streaming APIs provide ergonomic helpers for automatic transient recovery with explicit user opt-in and safe resource cleanup.
- Benchmarks demonstrate <=10% latency regression at p95 for typical bursty chat workloads and significant reduction in socket churn under 1k concurrent connections.

Notes: this ticket coordinates with runtime and networking teams for guidance on acceptable keep-alive intervals and pooling behavior across our hosted and dedicated deployments.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Discovery: spike run on connection churn in Python client when clients reopened per-request. Observed ~40% increase in CPU and many TIME_WAIT sockets under high concurrency. Logged findings in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/connection-churn-spike

2026-03-11 — Design sync: agreed on alignment goals with TS/Go owners (Anjali Patel, Tomasz Nowak). Decided to prefer conservative keep-alive (60s) and moderate pool sizes with per-host caps to avoid exhausting ephemeral ports for serverless customers.

2026-03-11 — Decision: adopt three-tier timeout model for each SDK: connect_timeout, idle_read_timeout, total_request_timeout. Will default total_request_timeout to 120s for non-streaming requests and require explicit opt-in for infinite streaming reads. This reduces surprising indefinite hangs.

2026-03-12 — Implementation notes (Python): switching to requests/urllib3 PoolManager with pool_maxsize=100, max_retries=2, keepalive=60. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/412 — includes integration test against local mock server that simulates network stalls.

2026-03-12 — Implementation notes (TS): use globalAgent/keepAlive agent config (agentkeepalive library), set keepAliveMsecs=60000, maxSockets=128, maxFreeSockets=64. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/298 — adds env var mapping and README examples.

2026-03-13 — Streaming ergonomics proposal: add StreamConnection.handleTransientErrors(retryPolicy) helper and expose AbortController integration for Node/browser. Must ensure on-abort handlers close underlying streams and drain KV caches to avoid memory leak. Proposal doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/streaming-retries

2026-03-13 — Testing: started benchmark harness comparing previous defaults vs new defaults under synthetic chat workload (200 concurrent users, 3 messages/second each). Early numbers: socket count stable, tail latency improved for retries, CPU down ~18% for Python spike test. Full results to be uploaded to dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/bench/sdk-transport-2026-03

2026-03-13 — Next steps: finalize config key names, land Python PR, then TS and Go follow. Schedule API/doc updates and add migration note for customers using custom transport configs. Coordinate with SDK release manager for minor-version bump and changelog entry.
